newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS-Prices end firm to weaker.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS-Prices end firm to weaker.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond markets ended the day unchanged to weaker on Friday, but showed no problems absorbing the large amount of new-issue supply from the past week, traders said.
High-yield bond prices dropped about one point, triggered in part by the weakness in the stock and Treasury markets.
"The market sold off 1/4 to 1/2 a point even before stocks tanked," one trader said. "(The fall in stocks) has added another half a point, so we're off about a point on the day."
Investment-grade bond spreads were unchanged on very low volume as investors ducked the volatility in Treasuries.

Traders reported Thursday's $3.0 billion debt offering from Raytheon Co was trading well in the aftermarket. The spread on the defense contractor's 30-year debt tightened to 73-73 basis points on Friday after being priced at 75 basis points, according to one trader.
Traders added that swap activity following Raytheon's four-tranche deal was minimal on Friday.

"Most accounts are so flush with cash these day they don't really need to sell anything to buy something," the trader said. "I'm sure some swapping was done for Raytheon, but I don't think it was a big percentage."
In new issue activity on Friday, Apache Corp priced $150 million in debentures (Baa1/BBB-plus) at a spread of 88 basis points via Goldman Sachs & Co.

Atlas Air Inc priced $150 million in 144a senior notes due '05 (B3/B-) to yield 10.75 percent via BT Securities Corp. The offering from the airline cargo company was increased from an original size of $100 million.
AMG Data Services Friday morning reported that U.S. high yield bond mutual funds received net cash inflows of $389 million in the latest recorded week, which ended August 6.
Another offering that saw interest in the secondary market was Western Resource's $520 million two-tranche deal, which was priced on Wednesday, traders said.

The 12-year tranche, priced at a spread of 95 basis points over Treasuries, tightened to a spread of 94-92 on Friday, he said. The seven-year tranche, priced at a 70 basis point spread, tightened to 70-68.
He added that the deal from the electric and gas utility saw particular interest from insurance companies.
Wall Street stocks tumbled on Friday, triggered by a sell-off in the Treasury market. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was 156.78 points lower toward the end of the day.
Treasuries slid sharply Friday, hurt by new supply, a battered dollar, hedge fund selling and technically driven trades, analysts said.
Toward the end of the day, the price of the benchmark 30-year Treasury tumbled by more than one point.
The price fell one point and 17/32 to 96-17/32, pushing the yield up to 6.64 percent.
-- Hugh Bronstein, U.S. Corporate Bond Unit, 212-859-1676
